items.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11
items.q: Brown had what? What's his name? Billy Lambert on drums

ctx.x: Well, I mean, there's a lot of those names you see from those fellas. I mean, they get away from you, you know. Sometimes they're nicknames, too. Yeah, and a lot of times they get away from you from being so far back, you can't remember.
And Brown's, and the bands of those days that were known bands, Brown had what? What's his name? Billy Lambert on drums and the other fella?
Yeah, Billy Lambert on drums, George guitar.

items.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11
items.q: Interviewer mentions: 'And I think it was Eagle Beak Lamb that was on drums.' Interviewee does not confirm or deny, nor does the interviewee mention Eagle Beak Lamb in their own turns.

ctx.x: That's all. I never had no big bands in there. There was only five men over the tracks in the real joint halls over there in the Tangle Palace. I worked there with Henry and Merritt Brunus. And I don't know who played piano. But I'll never forget that place over there. Remember Peg Leg?

Yeah, Anstead. Peggy Anstead. Yeah, an opera. I used to play for Merritt sometimes over there. They had a Jewish fellow piano player. Oh, really? I can't even place what was on. And they had Henry. Henry was playing trombone. I was playing cornet. And I think it was Eagle Beak Lamb that was on drums.
